subject: Urgent: tailored keepalive concession proposal for KiteWave renewal
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@kitewave.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@kitewave.com
Date: Mon, 1 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal questions + performance impact

Hannah,

We appreciate the partnership, but after the Q1 outages and the 28% usage spike our costs went through the roof. The renewal quote your team sent is a 15% increase vs current spend. Our finance and platform teams are pushing back — they need clearer compensation for the production incidents and an option to reset commitments for the next 12 months.

Concretely: can Redwood provide a one-time credit for the incident window, a temporary SLA uplift, and a shorter-term renewal (6 months) to evaluate stability before committing to the annual pricing? Without these concessions we will have to consider alternative vendors.

Can we get a short decision timeline? Procurement needs something before their board call on Apr 5.

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Head of Infrastructure, KiteWave
Phone: +1 415-555-0198

--
attachment: support-incident-log.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)
From: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@kitewave.com>
Cc: david.kim@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 1 Apr 2029 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal questions + performance impact

Alex — thank you for the clear ask and for sending the incident log. I’m really sorry you had that experience; we take outages seriously.

I’ve pulled together a preliminary save plan to discuss internally today:
- One-time credit equivalent to 20% of April usage to cover the incident window (applied at renewal).
- Six-month interim renewal at current effective rate (no increase) with the option to convert to annual at month 6.
- Temporary SLA uplift (99.9%) for the next six months; additional monitoring/tracing hooks enabled.

I’m looping in David (Sales Operations) and Marissa (Customer Success) to validate margins and operational commitments. I’ll aim to get an internal approval or list of required approvals by end of day Apr 3 so we can respond before your board call on Apr 5.

Would you be open to a 20-minute call tomorrow (Apr 2) to align the acceptance criteria for the SLA uplift and the conversion clause?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

--
attachment: usage-trend-2028-2029.csv (csv, 240KB)
From: david.kim@redwood.ai <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2029 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal questions + performance impact (internal)

Hannah/Marissa — quick take before I loop finance:
- One-time credit at 20% of April usage = reasonable for retention; gives a tangible customer appeasement.
- Six-month term at current rate is riskier (compresses ARR). If we do 6 months, require a priced option to convert to annual at prespecified rate or include a modest minimum commitment for conversion.
- SLA uplift for six months: OK if limited to monitoring/alerting + a one-time operational playbook; avoid long-term SLA exposure.

If legal needs to add contract language (conversion clause + incident remediation appendix) — flag now. Ben (revenue ops) — can we model the P&L impact and a guardrail (max total concession) by EOD? I want to keep the total concession below 18% of ARR impact for FY29.

Thanks,
David
Director, Renewals

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: david.kim@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 3 Apr 2029 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal questions + performance impact (internal)

Team — modeled scenarios attached (summary below). I’m okay with a limited concession but recommend approval guardrails:
- Option A (Customer-friendly): 20% one-time credit + 6-month hold at current rate + 6-month SLA uplift = estimated FY29 ARR haircut of ~11%.
- Option B (Balanced): 15% one-time credit + 9-month term at current rate + SLA uplift limited to enhanced monitoring = ~7% ARR haircut.
- Option C (Conservative): 10% credit + 6-month term but add a conversion commitment (3x monthly baseline over months 7–12) = ~5% ARR haircut.

If leadership approves Option A, we need an exec sign-off for the one-time credit and an authorization code for Finance to apply. Otherwise, Option B is my recommendation to protect bookings while showing good faith.

Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Operations

--
attachment: redwood-proposal-v2.pdf (pdf, 180KB)
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, david.kim@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: alex.rivera@kitewave.com
Date: Thu, 4 Apr 2029 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal questions + performance impact (to Execs for approval)

Hi Hannah/David/Ben — I’m elevating this to exec approval per our guardrail request. Summary for Execs:
- Account: KiteWave (Strategic, 3rd year, $1.1M ARR)
- Ask: One-time credit to cover incident impact + 6-month interim renewal at current rate + temporary 99.9% SLA uplift and operational playbook
- Rationale: High churn risk; customer engaged for platform modernization; strong expansion potential if stability proven.
- Finance impact: Option A = ~11% ARR haircut, Option B = ~7% (Ben recommends B)
- Recommended: Approve Option B (15% credit + 9-month hold + limited SLA uplift) unless exec prefers a stronger concession to expedite close before Apr 5.

Requesting an executive decision by EOD Apr 4 to honor the procurement timeline. If approved, Hannah will finalize contract language (conversion clause, incident remediation appendix) and Marissa will schedule the operational readiness call.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: ceo-office@redwood.ai <ceo-office@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, david.kim@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 4 Apr 2029 17:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: tailored keepalive concession proposal for KiteWave renewal — Exec decision

Team — after reviewing the account history and Ben's model, approved concession: Option B with a small tweak.
- Approve 15% one-time credit applied at renewal.
- Approve a 9-month interim term at current effective rate with a documented conversion option: customer may convert to a 12-month plan at month 9 at the agreed rate; conversion requires minimum 6-month notice and a 30% uplift clause if usage grows >40% in the interim.
- Approve limited SLA uplift (99.9%) for 9 months; operational playbook and two runbooks required.
- Conditions: Customer must sign the updated SOW with incident remediation appendix and commit to the conversion clause to qualify.

Finance: Ben, please issue authorization code AUTH-KW-0429 and update billing once the amended SOW is signed. Legal: draft SOW addendum and send to Hannah for signature. Hannah/Marissa: hold call with KiteWave tonight (Apr 4, 7:30pm PT) to close.

— Office of the CEO (on behalf of Execs)
